I had an extremely disappointing experience at this animal hospital when I brought my kitten in after she broke her toe. I was told that my only options were either amputation or surgery, and both options were quoted at thousands of dollars. As you can imagine, I was absolutely devastated. I was led to believe that these were the only ways to treat her injury, and I left feeling terrified that my kitten would either lose her toe or require an expensive surgery.

Because I was so overwhelmed, I decided to seek additional opinions before making such a life-changing decision. I took her to three different veterinarians, and every single one of them told me that neither amputation nor surgery was necessary. They all recommended a simple splint, explaining that the fracture should heal well with conservative treatment.

That is the route we chose, and after just three weeks in a splint, my kitten’s toe healed perfectly. She has no lasting issues and is back to running and playing normally.

Knowing how everything turned out makes my experience here even more upsetting. I spent days under immense emotional stress, believing I had to choose between amputating my kitten’s toe or paying thousands of dollars for surgery, when multiple other veterinarians agreed that a much simpler, far less invasive treatment was appropriate.

While I understand that different veterinarians can have different professional opinions, I was extremely disappointed that conservative treatment was never presented to me as an option or even discussed. It left me feeling as though the recommendations I received were driven more by expensive procedures than by providing a full range of appropriate treatment options.

I hope this review encourages the hospital to provide pet owners with more balanced information in the future. When families are making difficult medical decisions for their pets, they deserve to understand all reasonable treatment options so they can make an informed choice.
Thanks, Brenda, for trusting us with your pet's care! ❤️

My dog is a whole other story… I rescued her from the streets and she’s very aggressive at the vet. We have to fully sedate her to preform any sort of treatments on her. Dr. Cherrick is so kind and patient. She makes me feel like my dog isn’t a nuisance- she reminds me that my dog is great, simply very scared at the vet! It’s nice not to feel like my dog is evil. I’m writing this as both a long-time client and a concerned pet owner.

I’ve been bringing my kitty to North Avenue Animal Hospital since 2022. Over the years, there have been recurring issues with ‘missing’ or ‘over written’ records and canceled or not continued prescriptions, but today’s visit surpassed all of this.

I came in at 3:00 PM, specifically, for urinary issues related to FIC, a condition where delays in treatment can quickly become serious (& even fatal). Coconut had been visibly uncomfortable trying to use the litter box multiple times back to back, obviously stressing. I also mentioned them that I would love to talk about anxiety medication options for him in general as he is a high anxiety cat. Upon examining him I was told his bladder was very solid & hardened, yet when he was taken back to perform a urinalysis the staff also said they could not locate it because of how small it was all of a sudden??

Despite acknowledging his stress and knowing his past medical issues, I was essentially sent home with zero resolve. They refused to administer fluids, provide medication (they didn’t even mention or bring up my concerns regarding his everyday anxiety, let alone any sort of pain medication for the time being), or a treatment plan, then was told to return the next day AND pay another exam fee because the clinic was closing at 6:00 PM (its was 4:15 PM)  :) on top of paying a new client exam fee for the current visit even though we are long time clients.

Leaving a cat (or any pet) in urinary distress without literally any intervention or solution is 1. distressing and 2. medically unacceptable. I did not feel my concerns were taken seriously, nor did I feel coconut was treated with appropriate urgency.

When I told them that I was going to literally leave their office and go to another vet, they did not try to make anything right. No real understanding or empathy. SoOoo I immediately went to Bond Vet, where they WERE able to perform a urinalysis without literally any issue, provided a VERY different and more clear assessment of his bladder sitch, and sent us home with medication and next steps. The contrast in care was insane to say the least.

Obviously, I’m thankful I could get to another vet in time before the days end and that coconut is now being treated, but beyond disappointed that after years as a client, North Avenue Animal Hospital failed to provide basic continuity of care or support during a time-sensitive medical issue. I would urge other pet owners to think carefully before relying on this clinic in really any capacity.
The employee at the front was not very inviting and had an attitude when we asked for support.

North Ave Animal Hospital has always been an amazing care center for our pets (going on 20 years now), every single person there is compassionate and kind. It means a great deal to the animals that are in a stressful situation that every interaction is soothing. Couldn’t recommend more.
Thank you for the 5 stars!

Heartbroken and deeply disappointed.

Back in April, my dog Bruce was severely attacked by a German shepherd named Wolf— which turned out to be the manager’s own dog — while we were at North Avenue Veterinary Clinic. The situation was handled terribly. Despite the severity of Bruce’s injuries, the clinic did little to take responsibility or ensure proper follow-up care beyond covering immediate costs. There was no real accountability or empathy from management.

Bruce spent his last four months with a scar and a shaved side as a constant reminder of that incident. He’s now gone, and I have to live with knowing that his final months were marked by unnecessary pain and trauma that could have been prevented or better cared for.

I truly hope no other pet owner has to go through what I did. A veterinary clinic should be a place of safety and compassion — this experience was neither.

This feels like the neighborhood vet clinic that you see in movies - you recognize the folks who work here, and they remember you too. It has that community feeling and familiarity that is so hard to come by, the folks here deeply care about answering every question and helping as much as possible. Shout-out to Dr. Cherrick who has helped us through some particularly complex medical diagnoses, she's earned our trust completely. There's just nowhere else I'd rather go besides the people here.

As is echoed in other reviews, Dr. Cherrick is absolutely amazing. If it were not for her, the staff, and their continued care, we would go elsewhere as North Avenue Animal Hospital has been in an overall decline (and increase in prices) since being acquired by private equity. New policies and procedures are popping up that are obviously not solely for the benefit of our beloved animals. For this reason, I can no longer recommend them, as I have for almost 10 years.
Knowledgeable and confident, though, they don't do some things in-house
Thank you for the 5 stars!

I have been bringing my cats to North Ave for 5 years and am always so impressed by the level of care they receive! When one of my cats broke his leg they were absolute angels- from the doctor to the vet tech to the front desk they were so helpful during a really stressful time for us. The one who broke his leg hates going to the vet and even when he’s hissing at them they’re always patient, gentle and kind💕

I'll start with the positives. The wait times are low and the staff is very nice. No complaints there.

Now, let's get into the negative and just an overall problem with vets. Since I've been going here it's been a struggle to find a realistic common ground for caring for my pet. Everything is a $90 - $180 charge (just to step into their office) with little consideration of the circumstance. For instance, I've had to make make appts for my dogs eye checks that take under 2 minutes but somehow cost me over $100. Whereas the vet my family has been going to for years in STL, would just charge $20 or almost nothing for a re-check/barely any time spent appt.

The vet we saw was fine. But for an elderly dog, most of her problems I had to go to an ER vet anyways that they referred me to but would have me come in and then they would charge me for coming in to even get that referral.

Recently, I noticed that my chewy order for one of her meds wasn't being delivered and it turns out that they made a blanket rule that you had to come in and get the prescription and then pay for a stamp and then go to MAIL it to Chewy. Not only does this take twice as long and an extra cost but they lied and said the reason was that some people were getting the wrong prescription. Which makes no sense, because they have to "verify" the prescription before Chewy can send it. I knew there had to be a reason they were making people go out of their way (I am a single mom who works full time so this was crappy) and I found out today they are just trying to get people to use their online clinic instead. So if you have an elderly dog with several medications, can you imagine how many trips you have to make and how annoying this is? just so they can try to profit off you more.

I'm sorry but I just cannot stand for one more vet that's contributing to this money hungry grab and a huge contributor to the shelter crisis because people can simply not afford to pay for the pets.

This vet is not worth it.

They have been awesome. Our former vet quality on Western degraded so much when they got bought by some group. We were shocked when we discovered the friendly staff and people taking good care of our cat at NAAH, we really wish we would have discovered them earlier. We needed a USDA permit for moving with our cat and the team at NAAH clearly went above and beyond to help us (if you need such a permit, make sure you take extra time for processing as with the recent funding and personal cuts, people at USDA are overwhelmed and under staffed).
NAAH is a competent, kind and affordable veterinary practice.

Pup had a large , hard bump on hip. We were told she fell and it swollen (she didn't). Wife is in medical industry told me to go back as it was weird it was so hard and came out of nowhere.  Then, they Couldn't take a proper aspirate , nor read a x ray they took, said they saw nothing.  I Drove to Urbana champagne , got the aspirate done with results (2 times) , we emailed a friend  surgeon in Poland who quickly pointed out the calcification on one hip bone, which was caused by cancer, and quite obvious.  Hip bump..... look at hip bone on x ray, see an abnormality ????? Nope?? Many clinics send there x rays in for interpretation if you can't read them yourself..... if we hadn't taken action ourselves , my pup would have died of pain from bone cancer within a few weeks while they said it's all fine. We had her treated in Urbana champagne vet school for half the cost (lots of travel) , but lost time to treat the mass.  I've come here since our pups were born for ten years now . Felt like they did the same thing when she first tour her acl ..... here's some pain killers , it'll be fine , multiple visits and can't take a educated guess it's a torn acl , one of the most common injuries.  Just a money sucking leach of clinic while pups are in pain. Why do I have to ask a damn doctor in Poland to read tests they conduct !!!
Thanks so much for the review!

We’ve been taking our dog here since she was a baby! All the staff are so sweet, gentle, and helpful. My pup is so excited every time we visit them even after many many shots. Thank you for taking great care of my pup!!!
